conviction_note: The stock is down 44% since the 10 Aug print with no company news. It goes into the release with puts bid (+8.3 vol points of skew), at a 52-week low, and down 16% in five sessions. The ones that point down are the soft read from peer UTI on high-school starts, management's silence since August, and the structural lead and default headwinds management named itself. Pointing up are management's own Q3 starts guide, a revenue consensus that looks beatable, and a price already well below what the guide implies. All of it is inference or already in the August record, so p_up 47 on an abs move of 15 gives -0.9. The findings sum to -1.2. The two measurements agree in sign, and both are small because most of what is negative already looks priced.

The company guide is the bar there: Q3 starts back to low-double-digit y/y growth, high-school starts up more than 15%, FY26 starts +10-14%, FY26 revenue $590-600m, adj. EBITDA $76-80m, EPS $0.74-0.83, all reiterated 2026-08-10 (https://finviz.com/news/379811/lincoln-educational-services-reports-strong-second-quarter-financial-results-reiterates-full-year-financial-guidance). Comparable Q3 2025 starts base is about 6,445 (5,253 trades + 1,192 healthcare, excluding the 2,764 July 1 starts) and Q3 2025 revenue was $141.4m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1286613/000114036125041367/ef20058711_ex99-1.htm). Revenue and EPS consensus come from two or more agreeing sources (within about 2%), and the starts bar comes from the company guide, so neither is capped. The market's implied bar is clearly below the guide: $17.33 is about 22x the guided EPS midpoint and about 7x EBITDA.

That is not a crowded short, so there is no squeeze mechanism to shrink a negative for. Baseline skew is +8.27 vol points (downside paid). Put/call OI is 0.11, so open interest is overwhelmingly calls. The event-implied move is 13.66%, the straddle 16.16% at 99.5% ATM IV, and the ATM spread 11.8% of mid. On 2026-11-05 LINC fell 12.7% on 1.29m shares, the same day as UTI (-11.8%) and APEI (-9.9%) (Yahoo chart v8), so this was sector selling. findings.finding: Peer UTI reported its Apr-Jun quarter on 2026-08-05 and said Jul-Sep high-school starts in Auto/Diesel were 'tracking below plan'. It cut FY revenue guidance to $893-900m from $905-915m and cited softer high-school starts. Lincoln's Q3 guide rests on high-school starts rising more than 15%, and high school is about 40% of Lincoln's Q3 starts. So the direct peer's same-quarter high-school commentary is a negative read on the leg of Lincoln's guide most exposed to it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Starts are the line Lincoln trades on. The 2026-08-10 starts miss (+1% against roughly +10% expected) took the stock down 24.9% on a revenue and EPS beat. The 2026-05-11 print with Q1 starts up about 20% took it up 10.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Lincoln spoke five days after UTI, an analyst raised UTI on the 10 Aug call, and management still guided high-school starts above +15%, so the market has had this read since August. What is not resolved is whether Lincoln's own high-school recruiting overhaul offset the industry softness UTI described. If this were fully priced in the other direction, the stock would not be sitting at about 22x guided EPS with puts bid.
findings.independence: UTI's own release and the TipRanks summary (https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/universal-technical-institute-reports-mixed-q3-2026-results) are one document. UTI's stock has also collapsed: about $19.69 on 2026-11-06 against $40-51 in mid-2026, and Texas Capital downgraded it to Hold with a $25 target around late September (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/uti/). That points the same way for the sector, but it is not a Lincoln number.

findings.finding: Lincoln has said nothing about the August class since 10 Aug. On that call management promised the 'largest in our history' August class and said final numbers would be known about a week later. Since then there has been no 8-K or business update (EDGAR shows no 8-K after 2026-08-10), no investor-conference releases (unlike Sept 2025, when it presented at B. Riley, Lake Street and Barrington), and no buyback use despite $29.7m authorised to May 2027. There have been no insider purchases while the stock fell 44%. The 2026-10-19 scheduling release carried no starts preview; in Oct 2020 the company paired its scheduling release with a Q3 starts pre-announcement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior pre-release in the baseline window. In 2020 the starts pre-release (Q3 +15%) came out with the call notice (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2020/10/20/2110982/0/en/Lincoln-Educational-Services-Third-Quarter-Student-Starts-Climb-15-Schedules-Conference-Call-to-Discuss-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results.html).
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference from absence, and it is weakened because the company has not pre-released starts in recent years. Also, an open securities class action (lead-plaintiff deadline 2026-11-10) gives management a reason to stay quiet whatever the number is. The market has read the silence as bad. If it had read it as neutral, the stock would not have fallen a further 44% from the post-print $30.77.
findings.independence: The finviz headline list (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=LINC) shows no conference-attendance release since 2026-06-02 and no insider buys, and the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001286613/000114036126031995/ef20075880_10q.htm) shows the $29.7m buyback unused. These are different documents for the same absence.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-10, with July starts and the August enrolment pipeline in hand, management guided Q3 starts back to low-double-digit growth (about 7,100-7,200 against a comparable base of about 6,445) and high-school starts above +15%. It said a larger share of the August class had completed financial-aid packaging early, which historically means higher conversion, and that orientation attrition was lower than in Q2. It reiterated FY starts +10-14%. At $17.33 the price implies the market does not believe this guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When starts met the company's framing (Q1 2026 +19-20%, pre-announced at the March investor day) the stock rose 10.6% on the print. When starts missed it (Q2 +1%) the stock fell 24.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide is public, so this finding lands inside what the company already told the market, and that keeps it small. The price says the market has discounted it: about 7x guided EBITDA and 22x guided EPS for a company guiding mid-teens revenue growth, with analyst targets still around $50 (Lake Street, Rosenblatt and Barrington, Aug 2026). If the guide were believed, the stock would not be 44% below its post-miss close.
findings.independence: The 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001286613/000114036126031995/ef20075880_10q.htm) shows ending population up 10.4% comparable entering Q3, which supports the revenue line but not starts directly. Same company as the source, so not independent.

findings.finding: Revenue consensus of $152.4-155.5m implies only about +8-10% y/y against Q3 2025's $141.4m. Lincoln entered Q3 with ending population up 10.4% comparable, average population up 14.5% in Q2, and Q2 revenue growth (+22.4%) well above population growth because of pricing and mix. If population growth runs about 10-12% and revenue per student keeps rising, the implied range is about $155-160m, a modest revenue beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat revenue by about 2% and EPS by $0.06-0.07, and the stock fell 24.9% because of starts. Revenue beats have not paid when starts disappoint.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public, but the consensus sits low, and Northland's cut of Q3 EPS from $0.20 to $0.13 suggests analysts lowered numbers after the starts miss. This name does not trade on revenue, so the beat buys little.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 base from the company 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1286613/000114036125041367/ef20058711_ex99-1.htm). Consensus figures from Chartmill and Benzinga. Same company documents as finding 3 for the population figure.

findings.finding: Management named three structural reasons why starts converted poorly in Q2. First, some enrolees lost Title IV eligibility after defaulting on federal loans once collections resumed ('a few percentage points of enrollees'). Second, lead growth slowed, partly because of AI search tools favouring community colleges. Third, sales and marketing spend rose 31.1% on 'higher student acquisition costs'. None of these is a timing item, so each can carry into Q3/Q4 starts and the 2027 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The starts miss on these causes produced the -24.9% reaction on 2026-08-10.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since these were said on the call. What is open is whether they show up in the 2027 commentary, or in a cut to the FY starts guide if Q4 falls short. A first 2027 framing would be a guidance-scale event. If this were not already priced, the stock would still be near $30.
findings.independence: The 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001286613/000114036126031995/ef20075880_10q.htm) confirms the sales and marketing increase was due to higher student acquisition costs. That is the same company. There is no independent series on Lincoln's leads.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-05 the vocational and career-education group sold off together with no company news: LINC -12.7% (to $17.55 on 1.29m shares, about 2.6x its 20-day median), UTI -11.8%, APEI -9.9% (Yahoo daily bars). That leaves LINC down 16% in the five sessions into its print, at its 52-week low, with only 6.6% of float short.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for a sector selloff into a print in the baseline. After the August print the stock kept falling without further news.
findings.why_not_priced: The cause of the 11-05 group move is unidentified. It could be post-midterm (3 Nov) policy repricing, or a sell-side or peer read I could not find. It either lowers the bar (a relief setup) or carries information the sector has and I do not, so it is sized at 0.
findings.independence: UTI bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/UTI?range=1mo&interval=1d) and APEI bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/APEI?range=1mo&interval=1d) come from the same vendor.

findings.finding: Lincoln drew $26.0m on its $125m revolver by 30 Jun, bought the Melrose Park campus for $18.8m on 7 Jul with a $15m mortgage at 5.99%, and raised FY capex to $95-100m against $76-80m of guided EBITDA. It expects slightly negative FCF for the year and about $20m drawn at year-end. The money buys campus capacity: Hicksville opens Q4 2026, Rowlett Q1 2027, and East Point adds about 500 seats. Ending population up 10.4% corroborates demand for capacity, but the starts slowdown means that capacity is being built ahead of uncertain demand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The capex raise came with the August print that fell 24.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is disclosed, and leverage is low: total liquidity was $143m on 30 Jun. It matters only if a starts miss turns the capex plan into a cut-or-fund question at the print. Signed zero because the money funds visible capacity rather than covering losses.
findings.independence: The Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/379811/lincoln-educational-services-reports-strong-second-quarter-financial-results-reiterates-full-year-financial-guidance) gives the same capex and revolver figures. It is the same company.

baseline_tension: The mild negatives I found agree with the put skew and the -26% run-up, so they are probably already in the price. What cuts against the skew is that the price sits far below the company's own reiterated guide, so a guide that merely holds could produce a large relief move. That is why p_up sits near 50 rather than leaning hard either way.
